newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE wheat down again, rally now seen possible.
newsitem.headline: SFE wheat down again, rally now seen possible.

text.p: Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) wheat futures fell further on Friday in good volume, prompting some brokers to begin to look for a rally.
In SFE floor trades on Friday, market leader January 1998 fell by A$1.00 a tonne to A$169.00 on 23 traded lots. Twelve A$160.00 January put options also sold at a A$7.00 premium.
Friday's settlement prices were generally down by about A$2.00 a tonne.
In overnight SYCOM sales, 14 January 1998 lots sold at a steady A$170.00 a tonne.
Chris Gray of C, A & L Bell Commodities said a few large trading companies were willing to sell, although it was unclear who the buyers were.
Gray is looking for the possibility of a reasonably strong rally to emerge to take wheat back to the A$170.00-A$175.00 range.

This would be most likely if a market consensus backed the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics forecast of a significantly lower 1997/98 wheat crop of 16.2 million tonnes, he said. Australia's 1996/97 crop was a record 23.5 million tonnes.
